correctness.rationale: For n=6, disjoint coordinate matchings with four independent sign choices per matched pair give the exact cover face vector (60,720,960). Global sign reversal fixes no simplex setwise, preserves the pair-index orientation, and produces the quotient Delta-complex with (30,360,480) orbit cells. Independent reconstruction of every boundary incidence verifies ∂1∂2=0, connected quotient 1-skeleton and rank(∂1)=29. An independent sparse integral unimodular ±1-pivot elimination of the 360×480 ∂2 finds 270 unit pivots and a 90×210 residual consisting of exactly 120 entries +2 and 120 entries -2; dividing by 2 permits 15 further unit pivots, leaving a zero 75×195 matrix. Thus Smith factors are 1^270,2^15, with 195 zero columns. Separate modular ranks were 270 over F2 and 285 over F3,F5,F101. Since ker∂1 is primitive, H1=Z^(360−29−285)⊕(Z/2)^15=Z^46⊕(Z/2)^15; H2=Z^(480−285)=Z^195. Euler characteristic 150 agrees. All integer reduction steps are exact, not inference from finite-field ranks. The covering wedge assertion uses Wachs inflation theorem and is distinguished from the newly computed quotient.

value.rationale: This is a canonical, structurally motivated quotient: doubling the boundary of the six-dimensional cross-polytope and dividing by its global sign symmetry. Dimension six is the first cross-polytope dimension whose double has 2-cells; for dimensions ≤5 the corresponding quotient has dimension ≤1 and cannot acquire first-homology torsion. The exact 15 two-torsion generators therefore exhibit a natural first-dimensional obstruction to naive descent of an inflation wedge theorem and provide a concrete integral invariant for equivariant-topology comparisons. No arbitrary parameter selection, unmotivated tiny slice or general classification is claimed; standalone exact topology is worthwhile.
